title: Go SDK: stream-friendly generics helpers for typed decoding and structured output ergonomics
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Add a set of ergonomics-focused helpers to the Go SDK that make it trivial to decode structured model outputs into typed Go structs during both non-streaming and streaming responses. Deliverables: a small, well-documented package that exposes generic helpers (DecodeStructured[T], StreamDecode[T]) plus convenience types for common structured-output patterns, backward-compatible SDK surface additions, unit and integration tests, and examples that show retries, partial-decode fallback, and context cancellation semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Public API: DecodeStructured[T](io.Reader, opts...) -> (T, error) with clear error types for decode vs model-format errors
Streaming API: StreamDecode[T](ctx, io.Reader) -> (<-chan T, <-chan error) that yields typed partial/complete objects as they become available
Good ergonomics: few helper functions to cover >80% of structured-output use cases (single JSON object, repeated objects, jsonl, function-calling-like envelopes)
Retries: documented integration with existing SDK retry policy (idempotency considerations) and example showing how to combine with deduplication and backoff
Tests: unit tests for decoding success/failure, streaming cancellation, and memory/leak checks; integration test against a local stub service that streams fragmented JSON
Docs/examples: canonical example in examples/structured-output/showcase.go and README showing decoder usage, error handling, and migration notes
Benchmark: microbenchmark comparing encoding/json vs jsoniter in the hot path and guidance in docs; performance must be within 10% of current non-decoding path for typical payload sizes
Release: PR merged, changelog entry, and package published under github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/streamdecode
implementation_notes: Approach: implement a tiny package streamdecode that provides two primary helpers: DecodeStructured[T any](r io.Reader, opts...) and StreamDecode[T any](ctx context.Context, r io.Reader, opts...)

Streaming design: use a stateful incremental JSON tokenizer (encoding/json.Decoder with UseNumber or a small wrapper) to parse tokens as they arrive. For heavy workloads consider pluggable tokenizer implementation so we can swap to jsoniter later without API changes
Generics design: typed helpers should accept any user-defined struct type and return helpful decode errors (wrapped with context such as byte-offset and partial raw snippet) to simplify debugging

Partial-object handling: StreamDecode yields a typed value once a complete JSON object is parsed. For function-calling style responses (envelope with arguments), provide an Unwrap helper in the package
Fallback: if typed decode fails due to schema mismatch, allow an option to emit the raw map[string]any (as json.RawMessage string) so callers can surface helpful validation errors to users
Memory: avoid buffering whole response when streaming; allocate per-object buffers and reuse via sync.Pool for common sizes
Backwards compatibility: keep existing SDK Response types unchanged; this package should be an opt-in import with thin adapters in the main SDK for convenience

Retries and idempotency: structured decode helpers must be compatible with retries only for idempotent requests. Add examples showing how to safely rehydrate incoming stream state when retrying (use idempotency keys or dedupe tokens provided by server)
Error taxonomy: define errors.DecodeError, errors.StreamError, errors.PartialDecode which callers can type-assert against
Testing: create a test server that intentionally emits fragmented JSON tokens and occasionally injects malformed fragments to exercise fallback/partial-decode logic
progress_updates: 2024-11-02: Spike complete. Implemented prototype StreamDecode[T] using encoding/json.Decoder with buffered reader; confirmed we can parse fragmented tokens from a chunked HTTP response in unit tests.
2024-11-04: Design review with SDK leads. Decided to expose errors as concrete types for easier handling. Consensus to keep tokenizer pluggable for future performance swaps.
2024-11-06: Benchmarks: prototype median per-object decode ~1.12x slower than raw bytes path using encoding/json; added jsoniter shim to experiments for a fast-path switch.

2024-11-08: Implemented initial API surface and examples/showcase.go. Wire up CI integration test using local stream-stub. Found edge case where large nested arrays cause high allocations; added sync.Pool-based reuse for intermediate buffers.

2024-11-10: Internal review requested (PR opened). Added docs for retry guidance and idempotency notes. Need follow-up: finalize error messages, add more examples for function-calling envelope types. Assigned to Jordan for implementation of Unwrap helpers.

2024-11-12: Addressed CI failures: fixed race in test server, improved context cancellation propagation. Next: finalize API names (DecodeStructured vs DecodeInto), and prepare for SDK adapter PR. Targeting merge before 2024-11-22 release cut.
examples: Typed decode (non-streaming): var out MyStruct; err := streamdecode.DecodeStructured[MyStruct](resp.Body)
Streaming typed decode: ch, errs := streamdecode.StreamDecode[Event](ctx, resp.Body); for { select { case e := <-ch: handle(e); case err := <-errs: handleErr(err) } }
Fallback example: val, err := streamdecode.DecodeStructured[MyType](r, streamdecode.WithFallbackToRaw(true)) // returns raw JSON as string when decode fails
Retry guidance: Use SDK's retry middleware for request-level retries; avoid retrying mid-stream unless upstream supports resume tokens. Example in examples/retries/structured_retry.go
Function-calling envelope: use streamdecode.UnwrapEnvelope[FunctionCall](raw) to populate typed arguments and detect partial updates
